question: Which rooms can be entered directly through a door from the PHYSICAL EXAM room 1C18?
ground_truth: Seven rooms open directly onto the PHYSICAL EXAM room 1C18 through a door: 1C14 (HIST. / INTV.), 1C15 (PES ADMIN. OFFICE), 1C16 (ECG TEST), 1C17 (CHIEF AERO MED.), 1C19 (AUDIO), the corridor 1CC3 and the PROVIDER CUBICLES 1D16.

gold_cypher.base: MATCH (a:IfcSpace {Name: '1C18'})-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(:IfcDoor)<-[:BOUNDED_BY]-(r:IfcSpace) WHERE r <> a RETURN collect(DISTINCT r.Name) AS rooms
gold_cypher.topology: MATCH (:IfcSpace {Name: '1C18'})-[:CONNECTED_VIA]->(r:IfcSpace) RETURN collect(DISTINCT r.Name) AS rooms

verification: Base Cypher (rooms sharing a door through BOUNDED_BY) = topology CONNECTED_VIA = IFC door geometry (rooms whose footprint touches each door leaf, independent of IfcRelSpaceBoundary). All seven doors bound exactly two rooms; 1C18 has no open (virtual) boundary.

question: Which rooms can only be entered through the TECH. OFFICE 2D18, because their only door opens into it?
ground_truth: Seven rooms have a single door, and it opens into the TECH. OFFICE 2D18: 2D07 (SUPER), 2D08 (QA / HRD DIRECTOR), 2D14 (OPS SQUAD CMDR), 2D15 (1ST SGT), 2D16 (RMO DIR.), 2D17 (CREDENTIALS MGR) and 2D19 (READINESS NCOIC OFFICE).

gold_cypher.base: MATCH (r:IfcSpace)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(:IfcDoor)<-[:BOUNDED_BY]-(t:IfcSpace {Name: '2D18'}) WHERE r <> t AND COUNT { (r)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(:IfcDoor) } = 1 RETURN collect(DISTINCT r.Name) AS rooms
gold_cypher.topology: MATCH (r:IfcSpace)-[:CONNECTED_VIA]->(:IfcSpace {Name: '2D18'}) WHERE COUNT { (r)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(:IfcDoor) } = 1 AND NOT (r)-[:OPEN_TO]->() RETURN collect(DISTINCT r.Name) AS rooms

verification: Base Cypher = topology (CONNECTED_VIA, one door, no OPEN_TO passage) = IFC door geometry. None of the seven rooms has a virtual (open) space boundary in the IFC, so the door really is the only way in. 2D06, 2D10 and 2D20 also open into 2D18 but have a second door.

question: What is the combined floor area of all rooms that have a door onto corridor 1DC7?
ground_truth: Eight rooms have a door onto corridor 1DC7: the INTERACTION STATION rooms 1D28 (12.69 m²), 1D32 (12.75 m²), 1D34 (12.83 m²), 1D35 (12.83 m²) and 1D36 (12.71 m²), the PEDIATRIC WTS & MSRS room 1D31 (11.02 m²), the PEDIATRIC WAITING room 1D33 (12.74 m²) and the TRMT ROOM 1D38 (23.26 m²). Summing their Area values gives a combined floor area of 110.82 m².

gold_cypher.base: MATCH (c:IfcSpace {Name: '1DC7'})-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(:IfcDoor)<-[:BOUNDED_BY]-(r:IfcSpace) WHERE r <> c WITH DISTINCT r RETURN collect(r.Name) AS rooms, round(sum(r.Area), 3) AS total_area_m2
gold_cypher.topology: MATCH (:IfcSpace {Name: '1DC7'})-[:CONNECTED_VIA]->(r:IfcSpace) WITH DISTINCT r RETURN collect(r.Name) AS rooms, round(sum(r.Area), 3) AS total_area_m2

verification: Base Cypher = topology CONNECTED_VIA = IFC door geometry for the room set; areas from PSet_Revit_Dimensions.Area read with ifcopenshell sum to 110.817 m². 1DC7's open link to corridor 1DC6 has no door and is correctly excluded.

question: Which stairwells are closed off by a door of the '0915 x 2134mm Rated' type? For each, give its floor and the corridor that door opens from.
ground_truth: Four stairwells have a door of the '0915 x 2134mm Rated' type: 1BS2 on the First Floor (door from corridor 1BC4), 1CS3 on the First Floor (from corridor 1CC3), 2BS2 on the Second Floor (from corridor 2BC2) and 2CS3 on the Second Floor (from corridor 2CC4). The stairwells 1AS1 and 2AS1 of the third stair have no door of that type.

gold_cypher.base: MATCH (f:IfcBuildingStorey)-[:DECOMPOSES]->(w:IfcSpace {LongName: 'STAIR'})-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(d:IfcDoor)<-[:BOUNDED_BY]-(c:IfcSpace) WHERE c <> w AND d.ObjectType = '0915 x 2134mm Rated' RETURN collect(DISTINCT [w.Name, f.Name, c.Name]) AS stairwells
gold_cypher.topology: MATCH (f:IfcBuildingStorey)-[:DECOMPOSES]->(w:IfcSpace {LongName: 'STAIR'})-[v:CONNECTED_VIA]->(c:IfcSpace) MATCH (:IfcDoor {GlobalId: v.door_gid})-[:IS_OF_TYPE]->(t) WHERE t.Name = '0915 x 2134mm Rated' RETURN collect(DISTINCT [w.Name, f.Name, c.Name]) AS stairwells

verification: Base Cypher (door ObjectType) = topology (CONNECTED_VIA door -> IS_OF_TYPE type node) = IFC (IfcDoorStyle name via IfcRelDefinesByType, rooms touching the door leaf, storey via IfcRelAggregates). The fifth door of this type joins 1E05 and 1E06, not a stairwell.

question: What kind of wall separates the GAS STORAGE 1E15-A from the CENTRAL MECH. RM. 1E15, and what are its layers and total thickness?
ground_truth: The two rooms are separated by three wall segments of the type 'Basic Wall: Interior - Rated 1-HR (92mm Stud)', a one-hour fire-rated partition. Each segment is built up of 16 mm Type-X Plasterboard, a 92 mm Metal - Stud Layer and 16 mm Type-X Plasterboard, 124 mm (0.124 m) in total. The exterior wall that also bounds both rooms is their common outside wall, not the wall between them.

gold_cypher.base: MATCH (:IfcSpace {Name: '1E15'})-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(w:IfcWall)<-[:BOUNDED_BY]-(:IfcSpace {Name: '1E15-A'}) WHERE COUNT { (:IfcSpace)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(w) } = 2 CALL (w) { MATCH (w)-[:HAS_MATERIAL_LAYER]->(l:IfcMaterialLayer) WITH l ORDER BY l.LayerIndex RETURN collect([l.MaterialName, l.LayerThickness]) AS layers, sum(l.LayerThickness) AS t } RETURN collect(DISTINCT split(w.ObjectType, ':')[1]) AS wall_types, count(w) AS segments, collect(DISTINCT layers) AS layer_sets, round(max(t), 3) AS thickness_m
gold_cypher.topology: MATCH (:IfcSpace {Name: '1E15'})-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(w:IfcWall)<-[:BOUNDED_BY]-(:IfcSpace {Name: '1E15-A'}) WHERE COUNT { (:IfcSpace)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(w) } = 2 CALL (w) { MATCH (w)-[:HAS_MATERIAL_LAYER]->(l:IfcMaterialLayer) WITH l ORDER BY l.LayerIndex RETURN collect([l.MaterialName, l.LayerThickness]) AS layers, sum(l.LayerThickness) AS t } RETURN collect(DISTINCT split(w.ObjectType, ':')[1]) AS wall_types, count(w) AS segments, collect(DISTINCT layers) AS layer_sets, round(max(w.Width), 3) AS thickness_m

verification: Base Cypher (walls bounding exactly these two rooms, HAS_MATERIAL_LAYER; layer sum 0.124) = topology run (wall Width property 0.124) = IFC (IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage of the same three walls). Geometry check: all three wall footprints lie entirely in the strip between the two room footprints; the shared exterior wall overlaps it only at its end.

question: Which rooms can only be entered from outside the building, because every door they have is an exterior door?
ground_truth: Five First Floor rooms: 1E15 (CENTRAL MECH. RM., 1.83 m double exterior door), 1E15-A (GAS STORAGE, 1.83 m double exterior door), 1E17 (HAZ. STOR., 0.915 m exterior door), 1E20 (TRASH, 0.915 m exterior door) and 1E21 (FLAMABLE STORAGE, 0.915 m exterior door). Each has exactly one door, it is an exterior door, and no other room lies on its other side.

gold_cypher.base: MATCH (r:IfcSpace)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(d:IfcDoor) WITH r, collect(d) AS doors WHERE all(d IN doors WHERE d.Pset_DoorCommon_IsExternal = true AND COUNT { (:IfcSpace)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(d) } = 1) RETURN collect(r.Name) AS rooms
gold_cypher.topology: MATCH (r:IfcSpace)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(d:IfcDoor) WITH r, collect(d.is_exterior_door) AS ext WHERE all(x IN ext WHERE x) AND NOT (r)-[:CONNECTED_VIA]->() AND NOT (r)-[:OPEN_TO]->() RETURN collect(r.Name) AS rooms

verification: Base Cypher (Pset_DoorCommon.IsExternal + single bounded room) = topology (is_exterior_door, no CONNECTED_VIA, no OPEN_TO) = IFC (door leaf touches only that room, door type '... Exterior', boundary EXTERNAL; none of the five rooms has a virtual boundary or one of the 18 unbounded doors, which sit in toilets, 1AC1, 1DC1 and 1F01).

question: What is the minimum number of doors one has to pass through to get from the BIOMED MAINT. ADMIN. office 1E18 to the outside of the building?
ground_truth: Three doors: from 1E18 into the BMET WORK STATION 1E16, from 1E16 into corridor 1EC1, and then through the 0.915 m exterior door of corridor 1EC1. Continuing from 1EC1 into corridor 1EC4, which it opens onto without a door, and leaving through 1EC4's 1.22 m exterior door is equally short (also three doors).

gold_cypher.base: MATCH p = SHORTEST 1 (a:IfcSpace {Name: '1E18'})((:IfcSpace)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(:IfcDoor)<-[:BOUNDED_BY]-(:IfcSpace))*(x:IfcSpace)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(d:IfcDoor) WHERE d.Pset_DoorCommon_IsExternal = true AND COUNT { (:IfcSpace)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(d) } = 1 RETURN min((length(p) + 1) / 2) AS doors
gold_cypher.topology: MATCH p = SHORTEST 6 GROUPS (a:IfcSpace {Name: '1E18'})-[:CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO]->*(x:IfcSpace)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(d:IfcDoor {is_exterior_door: true}) RETURN min(size([r IN relationships(p) WHERE r:CONNECTED_VIA]) + 1) AS doors

verification: Base Cypher (door-only shortest path to a door with IsExternal that bounds one room) = topology (CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO walk to a room bounded by an is_exterior_door) = IFC graph search over doors (door geometry), virtual boundaries (cost 0) and exterior/curtain-wall doors: 3 doors, two equally short exits (1EC1, 1EC4).

question: Going from the SPECIMEN TOILET 1D14 to corridor 1DC3, which room do you have to pass through?
ground_truth: You have to pass through the SPECIMEN COLL. LAB 1D12: the toilet's only door opens into 1D12, and 1D12 has a door onto corridor 1DC3. The route is 1D14 → 1D12 → 1DC3, two doors.

gold_cypher.base: MATCH p = ALL SHORTEST (a:IfcSpace {Name: '1D14'})((:IfcSpace)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(:IfcDoor)<-[:BOUNDED_BY]-(:IfcSpace))+(b:IfcSpace {Name: '1DC3'}) RETURN min(length(p)) / 2 AS doors, collect(DISTINCT [n IN nodes(p) WHERE n:IfcSpace | n.Name]) AS routes
gold_cypher.topology: MATCH p = SHORTEST 6 GROUPS (a:IfcSpace {Name: '1D14'})-[:CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO]->+(b:IfcSpace {Name: '1DC3'}) WITH p, size([r IN relationships(p) WHERE r:CONNECTED_VIA]) AS doors WITH doors, length(p) AS len, collect(DISTINCT [n IN nodes(p) | n.Name]) AS routes ORDER BY doors, len LIMIT 1 RETURN doors, routes

verification: Base ALL SHORTEST door path = topology walk (CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO) = IFC graph search (door geometry + virtual boundaries): unique route, 2 doors.

question: Walking from the CERAMIC LAB 2C16 to the COMM. ROOM 2C15, which rooms do you pass through on the route with the fewest doors, and how many doors is that?
ground_truth: Three doors. The CERAMIC LAB 2C16 only opens into the PROSTH. LAB 2C17; from 2C17 you go into corridor 2CC5, and from 2CC5 into the COMM. ROOM 2C15. Route: 2C16 → 2C17 → 2CC5 → 2C15.

gold_cypher.base: MATCH p = ALL SHORTEST (a:IfcSpace {Name: '2C16'})((:IfcSpace)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(:IfcDoor)<-[:BOUNDED_BY]-(:IfcSpace))+(b:IfcSpace {Name: '2C15'}) RETURN min(length(p)) / 2 AS doors, collect(DISTINCT [n IN nodes(p) WHERE n:IfcSpace | n.Name]) AS routes
gold_cypher.topology: MATCH p = SHORTEST 6 GROUPS (a:IfcSpace {Name: '2C16'})-[:CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO]->+(b:IfcSpace {Name: '2C15'}) WITH p, size([r IN relationships(p) WHERE r:CONNECTED_VIA]) AS doors WITH doors, length(p) AS len, collect(DISTINCT [n IN nodes(p) | n.Name]) AS routes ORDER BY doors, len LIMIT 1 RETURN doors, routes

verification: Base ALL SHORTEST door path = topology walk (CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO) = IFC graph search (door geometry + virtual boundaries): unique route, 3 doors.

question: What is the shortest route, counted in doors, from the LOUNGE 2C22 to the CMDR OFFICE 2D11, and which spaces does it pass through?
ground_truth: Five doors: LOUNGE 2C22 → corridor 2CC1 → corridor 2DC2 → TECH. OFFICE 2D18 → SEC. WAIT 2D10 → CMDR OFFICE 2D11. The commander's office has a single door, into the SEC. WAIT room 2D10, and 2D10 in turn opens off the TECH. OFFICE 2D18.

gold_cypher.base: MATCH p = ALL SHORTEST (a:IfcSpace {Name: '2C22'})((:IfcSpace)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(:IfcDoor)<-[:BOUNDED_BY]-(:IfcSpace))+(b:IfcSpace {Name: '2D11'}) RETURN min(length(p)) / 2 AS doors, collect(DISTINCT [n IN nodes(p) WHERE n:IfcSpace | n.Name]) AS routes
gold_cypher.topology: MATCH p = SHORTEST 6 GROUPS (a:IfcSpace {Name: '2C22'})-[:CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO]->+(b:IfcSpace {Name: '2D11'}) WITH p, size([r IN relationships(p) WHERE r:CONNECTED_VIA]) AS doors WITH doors, length(p) AS len, collect(DISTINCT [n IN nodes(p) | n.Name]) AS routes ORDER BY doors, len LIMIT 1 RETURN doors, routes

verification: Base ALL SHORTEST door path = topology walk (CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO) = IFC graph search (door geometry + virtual boundaries; the open links 2CC1-2CC3 and 2DC1-2DC2 give no shortcut): unique route, 5 doors.

question: How many doors does one pass through walking from the JAN. CL. 1B16 to the CHIEF LOG OFFICE 1E05, and through which spaces does the shortest route go?
ground_truth: Five doors: JAN. CL. 1B16 → corridor 1BC3 → corridor 1BC4 (through a 1.0 m wide door) → corridor 1EC1 → TECH. WORK STATION 1E06 → CHIEF LOG OFFICE 1E05. The office's only door opens into 1E06.

gold_cypher.base: MATCH p = ALL SHORTEST (a:IfcSpace {Name: '1B16'})((:IfcSpace)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(:IfcDoor)<-[:BOUNDED_BY]-(:IfcSpace))+(b:IfcSpace {Name: '1E05'}) RETURN min(length(p)) / 2 AS doors, collect(DISTINCT [n IN nodes(p) WHERE n:IfcSpace | n.Name]) AS routes
gold_cypher.topology: MATCH p = SHORTEST 6 GROUPS (a:IfcSpace {Name: '1B16'})-[:CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO]->+(b:IfcSpace {Name: '1E05'}) WITH p, size([r IN relationships(p) WHERE r:CONNECTED_VIA]) AS doors WITH doors, length(p) AS len, collect(DISTINCT [n IN nodes(p) | n.Name]) AS routes ORDER BY doors, len LIMIT 1 RETURN doors, routes

verification: Base ALL SHORTEST door path = topology walk (CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO) = IFC graph search (door geometry + virtual boundaries; exhaustive enumeration finds no other 5-door route, the open links 1BC2-1BC3 and 1EC1-1EC2/1EC3/1EC4 give no shortcut). The route avoids the three-room door at 1BC2/1BC3/1B14.

question: Is there an indoor route, through doors or open passages, from the RECEIVING / STORAGE room 1E24 to corridor 1EC1? Which spaces can be reached from 1E24 that way?
ground_truth: No. Through doors, 1E24 leads only to the SEC. STORAGE 1E22, the ADP EQUIP SPACE 1E25 and the MECH. YARD 1F01 (through a 1.83 m double door of an exterior type). None of these has a door or an open passage to any other space, so corridor 1EC1 and the rest of the clinic cannot be reached from 1E24 indoors; the receiving area is reached from outside, through the mechanical yard.

gold_cypher.base: MATCH (a:IfcSpace {Name: '1E24'}) OPTIONAL MATCH (a)((:IfcSpace)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(:IfcDoor)<-[:BOUNDED_BY]-(:IfcSpace))+(x:IfcSpace) WHERE x <> a WITH collect(DISTINCT x.Name) AS reach RETURN '1EC1' IN reach AS reachable, reach AS reachable_spaces
gold_cypher.topology: MATCH (a:IfcSpace {Name: '1E24'}) OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[:CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO]->+(x:IfcSpace) WHERE x <> a WITH collect(DISTINCT x.Name) AS reach RETURN '1EC1' IN reach AS reachable, reach AS reachable_spaces

verification: Base Cypher (door-connected component) = topology (CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO component) = IFC graph search over door geometry and virtual boundaries: {1E22, 1E25, 1F01}. 1E24 is adjacent to corridor 1EC1 but no door or virtual boundary joins them.

question: Which toilets are directly adjacent to the consultation room 2C03 (CONSULT.), and from which corridor is each of those toilets entered?
ground_truth: Two toilets directly adjoin 2C03: the M. STAFF TOILET 2C07, entered from corridor 2CC3, and the W. TOILET 2C24, entered from corridor 2AC2. The W. STAFF TOILET 2C08 is bounded by a long wall that also bounds 2C03, but its footprint lies about 2.1 m away from 2C03, so it is not adjacent.

gold_cypher.topology: MATCH (:IfcSpace {Name: '2C03'})-[:ADJACENT_TO]->(t:IfcSpace) WHERE t.LongName CONTAINS 'TOILET' MATCH (t)-[:CONNECTED_VIA]->(c:IfcSpace) RETURN collect(DISTINCT [t.Name, c.Name]) AS toilets

verification: Topology ADJACENT_TO + CONNECTED_VIA = independent shapely re-computation from the IFC footprints (gap 0.124 m; shared edge 5.69 m for 2C07, 0.61 m for 2C24) + IFC door geometry. Base 'shares a wall' over-returns 2C08 (footprint gap 2.10 m).

question: Which rooms directly adjoin the PROVIDER CUBICLES 1D16 but have no door into it, and from which space is each of them entered?
ground_truth: Seven rooms adjoin 1D16 without a door into it: the COMM. ROOM 1C13 (entered from corridor 1CC1), the PES ADMIN. OFFICE 1C15 and the CHIEF AERO MED. office 1C17 (both entered from the PHYSICAL EXAM room 1C18), the JAN. CL. 1D17 and the TOILET 1D18 (both from corridor 1DC4), and the APPMTS room 1D20 and the GROUP IS room 1D21 (both from the WAITING / ACTIVITY AREA 1DC1). 1D16 also adjoins 1C18 and corridor 1DC4, but those two do have doors into it.

gold_cypher.topology: MATCH (a:IfcSpace {Name: '1D16'})-[:ADJACENT_TO]->(r:IfcSpace) WHERE NOT (a)-[:CONNECTED_VIA]-(r) MATCH (r)-[:CONNECTED_VIA]->(e:IfcSpace) RETURN collect(DISTINCT [r.Name, e.Name]) AS rooms

verification: Topology = independent shapely re-computation (all nine neighbours at gap 0.124 m, shared edges 1.6-5.5 m; 1CC1 touches only at a corner, 0.15 m) + IFC door geometry (each of the seven has one door). Base 'shares a wall' adds 1CC1, 1D19, 1D22, 1DC1 and 1C19 (gaps 0.3-8.5 m).

question: Which spaces directly border the MAIN MECHANICAL ROOM 2D05, and which of them can be entered from it through a door?
ground_truth: Six spaces border 2D05: the PROSTH. LAB 2C17, the ELECTRICAL room 2C18, the CENTRAL ISSUE room 2C19, the ADMIN OFFICE 2D09, corridor 2DC2 and the roof area 2R02. Three of them have a door into 2D05: 2C18 (its only door), corridor 2DC2 (1.83 m double door) and the roof 2R02 (1.83 m exterior double door).

gold_cypher.topology: MATCH (m:IfcSpace {Name: '2D05'})-[:ADJACENT_TO]->(r:IfcSpace) WITH m, collect(DISTINCT r) AS adj RETURN [r IN adj | r.Name] AS adjacent, [r IN adj WHERE EXISTS { (m)-[:CONNECTED_VIA]-(r) } | r.Name] AS with_door

verification: Topology = independent shapely re-computation (gaps 0.12-0.27 m, shared edges 1.9-16 m) + IFC door geometry. Base 'shares a wall' adds 2D10, 2D11 and 2C16 (3.8-8.5 m away).

question: How many staircases connect the first and second floors, and in which stairwell (room number on each floor) does each of them run?
ground_truth: Three staircases (type 'Stair: Concrete Pan - 180mm Max Riser 280mm Tread') run from the First Floor (elevation 0.00 m) up to the Second Floor (+4.57 m), each spanning about 0 to 5.7 m in height: one in stairwells 1AS1 / 2AS1, one in 1BS2 / 2BS2 and one in 1CS3 / 2CS3.

gold_cypher.topology: MATCH (s:IfcStair)-[:VERTICAL_ACCESS]->(:IfcBuildingStorey {Name: 'First Floor'}), (s)-[:VERTICAL_ACCESS]->(:IfcBuildingStorey {Name: 'Second Floor'}) CALL (s) { MATCH (:IfcBuildingStorey {Name: 'First Floor'})-[:DECOMPOSES]->(w:IfcSpace {LongName: 'STAIR'}) RETURN w.Name AS w1 ORDER BY (w.geo_cx - s.geo_cx)^2 + (w.geo_cy - s.geo_cy)^2 LIMIT 1 } CALL (s) { MATCH (:IfcBuildingStorey {Name: 'Second Floor'})-[:DECOMPOSES]->(w:IfcSpace {LongName: 'STAIR'}) RETURN w.Name AS w2 ORDER BY (w.geo_cx - s.geo_cx)^2 + (w.geo_cy - s.geo_cy)^2 LIMIT 1 } RETURN count(s) AS stairs, collect([w1, w2]) AS stairwells

verification: Topology (VERTICAL_ACCESS + nearest stairwell centroid, 0.2-0.8 m vs >24 m for any other) = IFC (stair flights' merged plan footprint overlaps exactly these two STAIR spaces by 10.5-11.4 m²; z range 0-5.7 m covers storey elevations 0.00 and 4.57). The base graph only has the stairs contained in the First Floor.

question: The PH TECH office 2B16 is next to a stairwell. If you take that stair down one floor, which first-floor stairwell do you arrive in, and which corridor does it open onto?
ground_truth: 2B16 adjoins stairwell 2BS2. The stair in it runs between the First and Second Floors, so going down you arrive in stairwell 1BS2, whose only door (of the '0915 x 2134mm Rated' type) opens onto corridor 1BC4.

gold_cypher.topology: MATCH (:IfcSpace {Name: '2B16'})-[:ADJACENT_TO]->(up:IfcSpace {LongName: 'STAIR'}) MATCH (s:IfcStair)-[:VERTICAL_ACCESS]->(:IfcBuildingStorey {Name: 'Second Floor'}) WITH up, s ORDER BY (s.geo_cx - up.geo_cx)^2 + (s.geo_cy - up.geo_cy)^2 LIMIT 1 MATCH (s)-[:VERTICAL_ACCESS]->(f:IfcBuildingStorey {Name: 'First Floor'})-[:DECOMPOSES]->(low:IfcSpace {LongName: 'STAIR'}) WITH up, s, low ORDER BY (low.geo_cx - s.geo_cx)^2 + (low.geo_cy - s.geo_cy)^2 LIMIT 1 MATCH (low)-[:CONNECTED_VIA]->(c:IfcSpace) RETURN up.Name AS upper_stairwell, low.Name AS lower_stairwell, c.Name AS corridor

verification: Topology (ADJACENT_TO -> nearest stair -> VERTICAL_ACCESS -> nearest first-floor stairwell -> CONNECTED_VIA) = IFC (shapely adjacency of 2B16: 2B18, 2BC3, 2BS2; stair 251180 overlaps 2BS2 and 1BS2; 1BS2's door leaf touches 1BS2 and 1BC4 only).

question: Which floors does the stair in stairwell 1CS3 serve, and on each of those floors, which corridor do you step into when you leave the stairwell?
ground_truth: The stair in 1CS3 serves the First Floor and the Second Floor. On the First Floor you leave stairwell 1CS3 into corridor 1CC3; on the Second Floor the same stair ends in stairwell 2CS3, which opens onto corridor 2CC4. Both stairwell doors are of the '0915 x 2134mm Rated' type.

gold_cypher.topology: MATCH (w0:IfcSpace {Name: '1CS3'}), (s:IfcStair) WITH s ORDER BY (s.geo_cx - w0.geo_cx)^2 + (s.geo_cy - w0.geo_cy)^2 LIMIT 1 MATCH (s)-[:VERTICAL_ACCESS]->(f:IfcBuildingStorey) CALL (s, f) { MATCH (f)-[:DECOMPOSES]->(w:IfcSpace {LongName: 'STAIR'}) RETURN w ORDER BY (w.geo_cx - s.geo_cx)^2 + (w.geo_cy - s.geo_cy)^2 LIMIT 1 } MATCH (w)-[:CONNECTED_VIA]->(c:IfcSpace) RETURN collect([f.Name, w.Name, c.Name]) AS floors

verification: Topology (nearest stair, VERTICAL_ACCESS, nearest stairwell per storey, CONNECTED_VIA) = IFC (stair 250693 footprint overlaps 1CS3 and 2CS3; z 0-5.67 m covers 0.00 and 4.57 m but not the roof at 9.25 m; stairwell door leaves touch 1CS3/1CC3 and 2CS3/2CC4).

question: How many doors does a patient pass through going from the VISUAL FIELD room 1C05 to the FITTING / DISP. room 1C04, and through which spaces?
ground_truth: Two doors. From 1C05 through its door into corridor 1CC2; corridor 1CC2 continues without a door (an open corridor junction) into corridor 1CC1; from 1CC1 through the door into 1C04. Route: 1C05 → 1CC2 → 1CC1 → 1C04. The two rooms share a wall but there is no door between them.

gold_cypher.topology: MATCH p = SHORTEST 6 GROUPS (a:IfcSpace {Name: '1C05'})-[:CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO]->+(b:IfcSpace {Name: '1C04'}) WITH p, size([r IN relationships(p) WHERE r:CONNECTED_VIA]) AS doors WITH doors, length(p) AS len, collect(DISTINCT [n IN nodes(p) | n.Name]) AS routes ORDER BY doors, len LIMIT 1 RETURN doors, routes

verification: Topology walk (CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO; OPEN_TO 1CC2-1CC1) = IFC graph search (door geometry + the virtual space boundary between 1CC1 and 1CC2): unique route, 2 doors. Base door-only graph finds no route at all (1CC2's doors lead only to 1C05, 1C06, 1C08 and 1C09).

question: What is the fewest number of doors one has to pass through to leave the building from the FAC. MGR. OFFICE 1E28?
ground_truth: Three doors: 1E28 → WORK ROOM 1E26 → corridor 1EC2 (two doors); corridor 1EC2 opens without a door into corridor 1EC1, which has a 0.915 m exterior door (the third door). Continuing from 1EC1 into corridor 1EC4, also an open connection, and leaving through its 1.22 m exterior door is equally short.

gold_cypher.topology: MATCH p = SHORTEST 6 GROUPS (a:IfcSpace {Name: '1E28'})-[:CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO]->*(x:IfcSpace)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(d:IfcDoor {is_exterior_door: true}) RETURN min(size([r IN relationships(p) WHERE r:CONNECTED_VIA]) + 1) AS doors

verification: Topology walk (CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO) to a room bounded by an is_exterior_door = IFC graph search (door geometry, virtual boundaries 1EC2-1EC1 and 1EC1-1EC4, exterior doors): 3 doors via 1EC1 or 1EC4. Base door-only graph reaches no exterior door from 1E28 (1EC2's doors lead only to 1E26 and 1E29).

question: A visitor in the CONF. / GROUP THERAPY room 2B3 has to go to the CMDR OFFICE 2D11. What is the minimum number of doors on the way, and which spaces does that route pass through?
ground_truth: Six doors. 2B3 → corridor 2BC5 (door 1) → corridor 2BC4 (door 2) → corridor 2BC3 (open connection, no door) → corridor 2BC2 (door 3) → corridor 2DC1 (open) → corridor 2DC2 (open) → TECH. OFFICE 2D18 (door 4) → SEC. WAIT 2D10 (door 5) → CMDR OFFICE 2D11 (door 6).

gold_cypher.topology: MATCH p = SHORTEST 6 GROUPS (a:IfcSpace {Name: '2B3'})-[:CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO]->+(b:IfcSpace {Name: '2D11'}) WITH p, size([r IN relationships(p) WHERE r:CONNECTED_VIA]) AS doors WITH doors, length(p) AS len, collect(DISTINCT [n IN nodes(p) | n.Name]) AS routes ORDER BY doors, len LIMIT 1 RETURN doors, routes

verification: Topology walk (CONNECTED_VIA|OPEN_TO) = IFC graph search (door geometry + virtual boundaries): unique route, 6 doors. A door-only search on the base graph returns 8 doors (via 2BC6, 2BC1, 2BC2 and the CONF. ROOM 2D20), because it cannot see the three open corridor connections.

question: The WAITING room 1C01 has no door. Which spaces is it open to, i.e. from where can it be entered?
ground_truth: 1C01 is open, with no door or wall in between, to the RECEPTION 1C02 and to corridor 1CC1, so it is entered from either of them. It has no opening to any other room.

gold_cypher.topology: MATCH (w:IfcSpace {Name: '1C01'}) WHERE NOT (w)-[:BOUNDED_BY]->(:IfcDoor) MATCH (w)-[:OPEN_TO]->(r:IfcSpace) RETURN collect(DISTINCT r.Name) AS open_to

verification: Topology (no door; OPEN_TO, from the virtual boundaries recorded on both spaces; also ADJACENT_TO method 'open', 3.1 m and 6.9 m of shared edge) = IFC virtual space boundaries of 1C01 (to 1C02 and 1CC1). The base graph only sees the walls to 1D11 and 1D13.
